final_report.root_cause: A missing/misnamed upstream configuration for the product-catalog service in the frontend-proxy (Envoy) configuration. The frontend-proxy deployment/pod does not have a configured/product-catalog upstream (no PRODUCT_CATALOG_* env vars, no cluster entry), so calls that require product-catalog could not be routed. Because the client-side call path detects the unreachable/misrouted product-catalog and returns a gRPC INTERNAL ('Product Catalog Fail'), those INTERNAL errors were propagated back through the frontend-proxy and observed in traces. The product-catalog application itself was healthy and did not emit errors — the failure was in routing/configuration at the proxy layer (likely introduced by a recent config change or missing config map/variable).
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Product-catalog pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and returned no ERROR application logs corresponding to the observed '13 INTERNAL: Product Catalog Fail' traces (priority #1). 2) The product-catalog Kubernetes Service exists (ClusterIP 10.96.113.130:8080) and endpoints are present (priority #2). 3) get_services_used_by(frontend-proxy) and the frontend-proxy Deployment/Pod environment show no PRODUCT_CATALOG_* env vars or cluster/upstream definition; product-catalog is not listed as a dependency of frontend-proxy, indicating the proxy is not configured to call product-catalog (priority #2). 4) Envoy in frontend-proxy started cleanly, loaded clusters/listeners, and its logs show no config/listener/cluster errors or local-reply generation — the proxy is operating normally and is likely forwarding upstream/client-side INTERNALs rather than generating them (priority #3). 5) Traces show frontend-proxy propagating error spans and messages '13 INTERNAL: Product Catalog Fail' despite product-catalog app health, matching a routing/configuration mismatch rather than an app crash.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 (epicenter) check confirmed product-catalog pod and app emitted no errors; the pod and its init container succeeded and there were no restarts or OOMs. Priority-2 (connection/config) compared frontend-proxy's configured upstreams to the product-catalog Service and found product-catalog missing from the proxy's configuration (no env vars/ConfigMap referencing it), while the product-catalog Service and endpoints were available — indicating a configuration mismatch in frontend-proxy. Priority-3 (proxy behavior) inspected envoy logs: the proxy started normally, had no cluster/listener errors, and contained no evidence it generated grpc-status=13 local replies. Correlation of these findings yields a causal chain: missing/misnamed upstream entry in frontend-proxy -> proxy does not (correctly) route calls to product-catalog -> client call path observes failure/unreachability and returns a gRPC INTERNAL ('Product Catalog Fail') -> frontend-proxy forwards/propagates that error to callers -> observed error traces. No further high-priority tasks are required to conclude this RCA; remaining lower-priority tasks (dependency health, trace-level deep-dive) could provide additional detail but are not needed to identify the root cause.
